title: Calibrate chat token estimation with provider-aware counts and conservative fallback

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Measured evidence from the TSK-0042 loop-unification parity tests (2026-06-12): on a multi-iteration turn where the provider reports no usage, the STREAMING path constructs each iteration's provider response with `finalChunk?.Usage ?? currentUsage`, feeding the prior aggregate back into CompleteUsage, while SendAsync estimates each iteration from scratch. Identical two-tool-call script produced: stream 17,756 input / 100 output tokens vs send 13,992 / 59. This divergence is PRE-EXISTING (both behaviors faithfully preserved by the unification) and now lives in ONE place: the streaming acquisition arm of MemoryChatAgent.ToolLoop.cs. When calibrating, decide whether to unify on estimate-from-scratch (send semantics) or provider-partial carryover — see the open question in the 2026-06-12 council page. A skipped-by-design note exists in ChatToolLoopParityTests.SendAndStream_ProduceIdenticalReplies_AcrossTwoToolIterations.
